quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: When is highway pavement most slippery?

options.text: After it has been raining for several hours.
When rain just starts.
After it has been raining for one to two hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: When rain just starts.
questions.explanation: Pavement is most slippery when rain first begins. Dirt and oil on the road mix with the water and create a slick film.

questions.question: You want to turn left at the next corner. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: Oncoming vehicles that are also turning left.
All vehicles coming toward you.
Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting to walk.

questions.correctAnswerText: All vehicles coming toward you.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to all vehicles coming toward you, including pedestrians and bicyclists on green lights.

questions.question: A pedestrian is walking on the road ahead. An oncoming vehicle is approaching. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and wait for the oncoming vehicle to pass before passing the pedestrian.
Keep your speed. The oncoming vehicle must stop for you.
Honk your horn to make the pedestrian move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait for the oncoming vehicle to pass before passing the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: Handle one danger at a time. If you need to pass a pedestrian but a vehicle is coming, slow down and let the vehicle pass first. Then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

questions.question: You are under 21. At what blood alcohol level can your license be suspended?

options.text: 0.15 percent or higher.
0.08 percent or higher.
Any amount.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any amount.
questions.explanation: Drivers under 21 cannot drive with any alcohol in their system. Any trace of alcohol will result in serious penalties, including a two-year license suspension.

questions.question: A large truck ahead is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. What may the truck do?

options.text: Complete its turn in either of the two lanes.
Swing wide to complete the right turn.
Stay in the right lane at all times while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swing wide to complete the right turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, the rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels. Long trucks need extra space to turn right safely.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Slow down and go carefully.
Stop as fast as you can.
Stop and only go when the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go carefully.
questions.explanation: At a flashing yellow light, slow down and proceed with caution. You do not need to stop completely.

questions.question: You are in the left lane with two lanes going your direction. Many vehicles are passing you on the right and a driver behind you wants to go faster. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in your lane.
Drive onto the left shoulder.
Move to the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane to pass or turn left. Use the right lane when driving slower than traffic around you or turning right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet.
Stop sign ahead.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road is slippery when wet. Slow down on wet pavement because it takes longer to stop.

questions.question: When driving in a construction zone, what should you do?

options.text: Slightly increase your speed.
Expect anything to happen.
Expect construction workers to move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect anything to happen.
questions.explanation: Construction zones are unpredictable. Drive very carefully to protect yourself, other drivers, and construction workers.

questions.question: Oncoming vehicles are on your left. Parked vehicles are on your right. Where should you steer?

options.text: Closer to the oncoming vehicles.
Closer to the parked vehicles.
Between the oncoming and parked vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Between the oncoming and parked vehicles.
questions.explanation: When you have oncoming vehicles on one side and parked vehicles on the other, steer down the middle between them.

questions.question: At a red traffic light with a green arrow, when can you proceed in the direction of the arrow?

options.text: After you come to a complete stop.
When the light changes.
When you are in the correct lane and the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are in the correct lane and the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go in that direction if you are in the correct lane and the road is clear. This rule applies whether the arrow appears alone or with other signals.

questions.question: When traffic is moving at 50 to 55 mph, you are least likely to have an accident if you:

options.text: Drive a few miles per hour faster than other vehicles.
Drive at the same speed as other vehicles.
Drive a few miles per hour slower than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Match your speed to the other traffic on the road, as long as it is within the speed limit. Vehicles moving at the same speed in the same direction cannot hit each other. Accidents happen when some vehicles drive faster or slower than others.

questions.question: When you see an octagonal sign, you must:

options.text: Slow down.
Stop.
Turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An octagonal sign always means stop. Come to a complete stop, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red light at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Slow down and let others go first.
Slow down and drive carefully through.
Stop completely, look both ways, and go when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, look both ways, and go when safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When driving in fog, which headlights should you use?

options.text: High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect back at you, making it harder to see.

questions.question: Which of these is a dangerous habit in work zones?

options.text: Following another vehicle too closely.
Not watching for workers and equipment.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: In work zones, slow down and keep a safe distance from other vehicles. Pay attention to workers and equipment.

questions.question: To avoid losing traction on wet roads, you should:

options.text: Make sharp turns.
Brake hard.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on wet roads to prevent hydroplaning. Keep your tires in good condition. If you lose control, ease off the gas, do not brake, keep the car straight, and let it slow down on its own.

questions.question: What does a "No passing zone" sign tell you?

options.text: Speed up a little.
It is not safe to pass another vehicle here.
Keep a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is not safe to pass another vehicle here.
questions.explanation: Do not pass in a "No passing zone." You are in an area where you cannot see ahead clearly, making it unsafe to pass.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines mean:

options.text: No one may pass in either direction.
Both directions may pass.
Only the right lane may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: No one may pass in either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use your turn signal?

options.text: Only when leaving the curb.
Only when pulling up to the curb.
When pulling up to or leaving the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pulling up to or leaving the curb.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal both when pulling up to a curb and when leaving it.

questions.question: You should not enter an intersection if you know you will block it when the light turns red:

options.text: Under any circumstances.
Unless you entered the intersection on a yellow light.
Unless you entered the intersection on a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under any circumstances.
questions.explanation: Even if the light is green, you must not enter an intersection unless you can drive completely across before the light turns red. If you block the intersection, you can get a ticket.

questions.question: You see a green light ahead, but traffic is blocking the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Partially enter the intersection to claim your right-of-way.
Wait until you can drive completely across the intersection.
Enter the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can drive completely across the intersection.
questions.explanation: Even if your light is green, do not enter an intersection unless you can drive completely through it before the light turns red. If you block the intersection, you can get a ticket.

questions.question: A double solid yellow line down the center of the road means passing is:

options.text: Allowed from both directions.
Allowed only from your direction.
Not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means traffic is moving in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.question: This white sign means:

options.text: The crossing is controlled. Drive at your normal speed.
Look, listen, and be ready to stop if needed.
Stop at the tracks and wait for permission to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: When approaching a railroad crossing, look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop. Wait for any trains to pass before you cross.

questions.question: Motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see. Therefore, you should:

options.text: Slow down when driving.
Check your surroundings constantly.
Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your surroundings constantly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and can hide in your blind spot. You must always be alert and looking for motorcycles, mopeds, and scooters.

questions.question: You should use your horn when:

options.text: Another vehicle is in your way.
It may help prevent a crash.
Another driver makes a mistake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may help prevent a crash.
questions.explanation: Only use your horn when necessary to avoid crashes. Do not use it to tell slower drivers to go faster or move out of your way.

questions.question: When a blind pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane is crossing the street:

options.text: You must always yield the right-of-way.
You must tell them where to cross.
You only have to yield at intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Blind or partially blind pedestrians carry a white cane or use a guide dog. You must always yield the right-of-way to them.

questions.question: In fog or mist, do not use high beam headlights because:

options.text: The light bounces back into your eyes.
Other vehicles might not see you.
Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light bounces back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, high beam headlights bounce the light back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: Leave extra space in front of your vehicle when following a:

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger vehicle.
Motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space when behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop faster than cars. You need room to stop if the rider brakes suddenly. Also, motorcycles have only one tail light and are hard to see at night.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should always:

options.text: Stop, listen, and go slowly.
Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
Slowly pass vehicles that seem to be stopped for no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
questions.explanation: At these locations, look to the left and right sides of your vehicle to make sure no one is coming into your path.

questions.question: Which statement is true about roadwork zones?

options.text: Fines for violations in work zones are the same as fines for normal traffic violations.
You must slow down in the cone zone.
Slow down only if you see workers present.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must slow down in the cone zone.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop for highway equipment. Driving carefully through work zones keeps drivers, pedestrians, cyclists, and road workers safe.

questions.question: A vehicle is coming toward you at night with high beams on. You cannot see the road. What should you do?

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at the headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the oncoming vehicle from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: When should your wheels NOT be pointed straight ahead?

options.text: When waiting to turn left at a traffic light.
When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
When parked on a level roadway with no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.
questions.explanation: Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. This prevents you from sliding into oncoming traffic if hit from behind. On a hill, turn your wheels so the car will not roll into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: You are parking uphill on a road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking uphill or downhill on a road with no curb, turn your wheels so the car will roll away from the center of the road if the brakes fail.

questions.question: You see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down because the lane ends ahead.
Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and keep your current speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: Signs and message boards warn you about workers, slow equipment, and closed lanes ahead. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What is the correct order of traffic lights from top to bottom?

options.text: Red, yellow, green.
Red, green, yellow.
Green, red, yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Red, yellow, green.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions ahead. This sign warns drivers that traffic signals are at the next intersection.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of the road. How do you prevent it in wet weather?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a constant speed.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slow down on wet pavement to prevent hydroplaning.

questions.question: A person is crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog. What should you do?

options.text: Stop until the person is far away from your path.
Honk your horn as you pass them.
Drive carefully around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is far away from your path.
questions.explanation: Stop for a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog until they are well away from your vehicle. Always give blind pedestrians the right-of-way.

questions.question: When driving through a construction zone, you should:

options.text: Stop to watch the workers.
Decrease the distance between you and the car ahead.
Pass carefully and do not stare at the construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass carefully and do not stare at the construction.
questions.explanation: Do not stare at unusual sights. This slows traffic and causes congestion. Drive through the construction zone without looking at the workers.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is using its siren and flashing lights. How do you yield the right-of-way?

options.text: Move to the right edge of the road and stop.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Stop immediately, even in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Move to the right edge of the road and stop for any emergency vehicle using its siren and flashing lights. Avoid stopping in an intersection. You can move again after the emergency vehicle has passed.
